scope: Kebu Liguey (K066) acceptance case 4: employer/recruiter workflow (authorized posting + tenant-scoped applicant review, honest decision/status handling), plus the minimum of case 3 (submit/withdraw) needed to make review real rather than reviewing zero applications forever. Real public work discovery (case 2, needs a service-role public route filtering status='published', modeled on business_events' precedent) and the SAFA connected journey (case 5) remain separate, not-yet-started acceptance cases — this slice does not build a public listings page.

mappedBeforeAnyCode.method: Background Explore agent mapped the employer/tenant-isolation pattern, authorized-posting-with-public-visibility precedent, reviewer-decision precedent, and assertBusinessManager's role-list consistency before any schema or code was written.
mappedBeforeAnyCode.employerEntity: Confirmed: businesses/business_members (archived-only schema, already repaired for its own RLS recursion earlier the same day) is the only tenant entity in the codebase — no separate employer-account concept exists or was invented.
mappedBeforeAnyCode.tenantIsolationPrecedent: Every business_* table follows the same shape: a SELECT policy exists()-checking business_members for any active member, and a stricter write policy additionally checking role membership. job_listings/job_applications follow this exact shape rather than inventing a new one.
mappedBeforeAnyCode.publicVisibilityPrecedent: Confirmed no business_* table has an anon/public RLS SELECT policy anywhere. Public reach for business-owned content (business_events) goes through a service-role API route filtering status in application code, never through RLS opened to anon. job_listings follows this: no anon SELECT policy; a public discovery route is deliberately deferred to case 2, not built here.
mappedBeforeAnyCode.reviewerDecisionPrecedent: event_registrations + its manager-gated PATCH route is the only existing 'reviewer decides, submitter is informed' shape, but it has no submitter-side read-back at all (registrants are anonymous guests, not auth.users rows). job_applications had to design the submitter-read case fresh: applicant_user_id references auth.users, RLS lets the applicant read their own row directly.
mappedBeforeAnyCode.assertManagerMismatchConfirmed: lib/business/assert-manager.ts allows ['founder','administrator','store_manager','manager','creative'] — confirmed inconsistent with both the business_members DB role check constraint (no 'manager' or 'creative' role exists in the base, confirmed-live constraint) and with the two OTHER inline copies of this same check (app/api/businesses/[id]/events/route.ts and its registrations route), which both use only ['founder','administrator','store_manager']. Deliberately did NOT reuse any of the three existing variants verbatim: lib/liguey/assert-employer-manager.ts defines its own explicit allow-list matching the two DB-constraint-consistent copies, rather than inheriting the ambiguity into a fourth variant. The ambiguity itself is not resolved here — a separate, pre-existing inconsistency across three call sites, out of scope for this slice.

schema.migration: supabase/migrations/20261016190000_liguey_job_listings_applications.sql — job_listings (business-owned, public_id reserved for case 2's future public route, status draft/published/closed/archived) and job_applications (listing_id + denormalized business_id + applicant_user_id, status submitted/reviewed/accepted/declined/withdrawn, unique(listing_id, applicant_user_id) preventing duplicate submissions).
schema.crossTableRlsBugFoundAndFixed: Writing the real-SQL regression test surfaced a genuine design bug before it shipped, distinct from the two RLS-recursion-class bugs found earlier the same day for Rooms/business_members: job_applications' INSERT policy needed to verify 'is this listing actually published', but an applicant is never a business_members row for the hiring business and job_listings has no public SELECT policy — so the WITH CHECK subquery would see zero rows for every applicant, regardless of whether the listing was genuinely published, making it impossible for anyone to ever apply. Fixed with a narrowly-scoped SECURITY DEFINER helper, private.is_published_job_listing(listing_id, business_id), that answers only a bare boolean ('does a published listing with this id/business_id exist') and leaks no other field — confirmed to fail without the fix and pass with it before trusting the result.
schema.decisionIntegrity: decided_at/decided_by are never client-writable — not granted to authenticated at all, mirroring worker_profiles.verified_at's convention. A BEFORE UPDATE trigger (private.stamp_job_application_decision) stamps them automatically only when status transitions into accepted/declined, and clears them if a decision is reverted, so 'who decided and when' can never be forged by either the applicant or the business side.
schema.identityGuard: A guard trigger blocks reassigning listing_id/business_id/applicant_user_id after creation, mirroring the workspace_item/library_node convention — though verified during testing that the column-grant layer (business_id/listing_id/applicant_user_id are simply never granted for UPDATE) actually blocks this even earlier than the trigger does; the trigger remains as defense-in-depth.
schema.authorizationLayering: Listing creation/update and application decisions are gated at both the RLS layer (role in ('founder','administrator','store_manager')) and the application layer (lib/liguey/assert-employer-manager.ts, called before any mutating route proceeds) — verified a non-manager is rejected at both layers, not just one.

apiAndUi.employerRoutes: app/api/liguey/employers/[businessId]/listings/route.ts (GET list, POST create with public_id collision retry mirroring newEventPublicId's pattern), app/api/liguey/employers/[businessId]/listings/[listingId]/route.ts (GET one listing + its applications, PATCH update/publish/close/archive), app/api/liguey/employers/[businessId]/listings/[listingId]/applications/[applicationId]/route.ts (PATCH a manager's decision).
apiAndUi.applicantRoutes: app/api/liguey/applications/route.ts (GET own applications with listing titles joined, POST submit, PATCH withdraw).
apiAndUi.ui: app/business/[id]/liguey/page.tsx + app/components/liguey/liguey-employer-panel.tsx (manager-gated at the page level with a redirect, not just hidden — listing creation, status changes, and per-listing applicant review with accept/decline/mark-reviewed). app/liguey/applications/page.tsx + app/components/liguey/liguey-applications-panel.tsx (the worker's own application list with status and a withdraw button). app/liguey/page.tsx updated to link to both, including listing businesses the signed-in user manages, so this is genuinely reachable rather than a hidden route.

verifiedScenarios.realSqlPGliteTests: tests/liguey/job-listings-applications.local.test.ts — 14 real-SQL PGlite cases against the actual migration SQL applied verbatim, gated on KEBU_LOCAL_PGLITE_ROOT, run explicitly: a manager-role member can create a listing, a plain employee cannot (but can still read, including drafts); a stranger business cannot read another business's listings at all; a worker cannot apply to a draft listing, can apply to a published one, cannot apply twice, and cannot spoof a mismatched business_id; the applicant and any active business member (not only managers) can read an application, a different applicant cannot; a manager's accept/decline stamps decided_at/decided_by automatically and the applicant sees the decision on their own read-back; an applicant can withdraw their own application but cannot set any other status; a plain employee cannot decide on an application (RLS silently excludes the row, confirmed not to throw, matching this codebase's existing owner-scoped-update convention); the application's business cannot be reassigned after creation (blocked at the column-grant layer before RLS or the trigger even run).
verifiedScenarios.mockedRouteTests: tests/liguey/employer-listings-route.test.ts (6), employer-listing-detail-route.test.ts (6), application-decision-route.test.ts (5), applicant-applications-route.test.ts (7) — first-ever coverage for these four new route files, covering manager-gating, invalid payloads, 404/409/403 edge cases, and cross-origin rejection.

fullSuiteResult: typecheck 0 errors; lint 0 errors/349 warnings (unchanged); vitest 6,004 passed/244 skipped (+25/+14 vs. the case-1 checkpoint — the 14 new skips are the real-SQL file, run explicitly with KEBU_LOCAL_PGLITE_ROOT set and all 14 passed; same 3 pre-existing hosted-QA-only failures); build confirmed separately.
stillOpen: Real public work discovery (case 2) is not built — no service-role public listings route or public page exists yet, so an applicant can only apply to a listing whose id/business_id they already have (e.g. via a direct link), not one they discovered through the product. The SAFA connected journey (case 5), deeper Network/Rooms integration (case 6), EN/FR/Wolof coverage (case 7), and real browser verification all remain explicitly open. The pre-existing assertBusinessManager role-list ambiguity across three call sites is confirmed but not resolved in this slice. Genuine hosted Supabase Auth/RLS acceptance remains open, as for every slice this session.
